Create ONE publication architecture figure matching the ATTACHED USER REFERENCE IMAGE's graphic language, not its method: compact wide landscape ~2.4:1, three adjoining pastel panels, upper-left pale cyan for feature modeling, lower-left pale lime for tokens, right pale peach for decoding. White outer margin, sharp thin black orthogonal arrows, small colored rectangular modules and trapezoidal encoder/decoder blocks, stacked feature-map rectangles, tiny token squares, bold sans-serif panel captions, readable English labels. No giant title, no spacious poster design, no gradients, no shadows, no decorative art. Rich but controlled dense technical figure like the reference. Do NOT import text prompts, panoptic/instance outputs, or contrastive loss from reference. This is organ semantic segmentation. Three panels captioned (a), (b), (c). Training-only loss connections magenta dashed, inference black. Every computation arrow must follow graph below.Shared modules: input CT icon branches into ViT (MAE) and shallow CNN. ViT produces z. Pixel decoder combines z with CNN shallow skips S8 and S4 to produce P16,P8,P4. Organ pathway z -> OrganCollector -> TGEnc -> 20 organ tokens T. A small bottom reconstruction strip branches ORIGINAL T -> AHER -> Fusion -> Shared reconstruction decoder -> reconstructed image. This reconstruction path is auxiliary and separate from segmentation. Figure E cross-attention. Panel (a) Shared multi-scale features. Panel (b) Organ query formation: T -> Mean pool -> Query projection + Slot ID -> q. Panel (c) Query-conditioned masks: q and original P4 enter Cross-attention then FFN yielding q'. q' and unchanged P4 enter cosine dot circle -> Upsample -> Organ mask. Original P4 bypass visibly goes to dot, NOT updated P4. A dashed inset expands Cross-attention + FFN. Single semantic organ mask output, not instances. Label feature scales P16 (1/16), P8 (1/8), P4 (1/4).
